name: TX-12
label: Safe R

key_factors: District's Republican lean of about 11 points on the partisan index
Incumbent Craig Goldman running with a large financial advantage ($1.5M on hand)
Prediction markets price Goldman at roughly 94% to win
No public polling or expert ratings available for the race
model.rationale: The seat's 11-point Republican lean, Goldman's incumbency and dominant fundraising, and markets pricing him near 94% all point to a comfortable but not automatic Republican hold. With no polls to sharpen the estimate, uncertainty stays wide, keeping this at Likely R rather than Safe R.
model.watch: Any credible polling showing the Democrat within single digits, or a major late scandal or funding surge, would move the race toward Tossup.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
TX-12 is a solidly Republican Fort Worth–area seat with an 11-point Republican lean on the partisan index. Incumbent Craig Goldman, first elected in 2024, is running for reelection and holds a commanding financial position, with about $1.5 million on hand against a Democratic challenger with no reported fundraising. Outside spending has been minimal and one-sided in Goldman's favor.

No public general-election polls or expert ratings are available for this race, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals and money. Prediction markets give Goldman roughly a 94% chance of winning. The forecast expects a Republican win by around 15 points, with meaningful uncertainty given the absence of polling.
